spec_match.rationale: The code sample now teaches the spec's depthTypeRequest: ["smooth"] sequence (fixed this pass; it previously showed a scalar depthType member the spec does not define) alongside pauseDepthSensing()/resumeDepthSensing(), but the stage is a canvas simulation that never calls a real XR surface.

interactive.rationale: The raw/smooth/off mode toggle drives the simulated depth render and stats live — CDP click on 'smooth depth' flipped the active mode and updated fps 60 / per-frame cost 3x.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Concept page lede restates and delivers on the framing used in the feature index card.

edge_cases.rationale: Only the happy simulated path is demonstrated — no navigator.xr feature detection and no visible unsupported/error branches (carried from the 2026-06-01 critique; unchanged by this pass's one-line snippet fix).

references.rationale: Page cites chromestatus.com/feature/5074096916004864 (the feature's verified id) and the spec.

conformance.rationale: Only the feature-level interface-existence suite covers this page; no assertions capture the raw-vs-smooth or pause/resume contract this concept teaches (existing suites are immutable; not touched).

runtime_evidence.rationale: This pass (headless Chromium 141 via CDP, desktop 1280x1600 + mobile 360x740 DPR3): page loads clean (only the environmental fonts.googleapis.com failure), the corrected snippet text is served, the smooth toggle was driven and updated the stats, and no horizontal overflow on either class — but only the primary control was exercised, not the full control matrix.

telemetry_health.rationale: No showcaseTelemetry asserts anywhere on the page.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout and the toggle's dark active state pairs background with color (rules 5 and 6).

accessibility.rationale: Controls are native buttons, but the canvases carry generic labels ('Rgb canvas', 'Depth canvas'), the active mode is conveyed by class styling rather than aria-pressed, and the changing stats have no live-region equivalent; the accessibility tree was not inspected this pass.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 1280x1600 or 360x740 DPR3 (CDP emulation, screenshots taken), but touch operation of every control and the full parity checklist were not exercised this pass.

openQuestions.title: Demonstrate failure and edge-case branches
openQuestions.detail: Add visible branches for the unsupported/unavailable paths: a navigator.xr + isSessionSupported('immersive-ar') probe with an honest 'no XR on this device — simulation below' banner, and surface what a rejected depth-sensing feature request looks like. Today only the simulated happy path is reachable.

openQuestions.title: Expose mode state and stats non-visually and add telemetry
openQuestions.detail: Give the raw/smooth/off toggle aria-pressed semantics, name the canvases meaningfully, mirror the fps/cost/noise stats through a polite live region or descriptive text, and record a showcaseTelemetry assert after a mode switch.

guidanceConsulted.query: aria-live region announcing updated results after select change
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Dynamic result updates driven by controls should be announced through appropriate live semantics.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Exception for this pass: the only change made here was a one-line factual fix to the code sample (depthType -> depthTypeRequest sequence), so no UI restructuring was done; the missing live semantics are recorded as an open question instead.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: CDP verification limited to the corrected snippet text, the smooth-toggle interaction, console, and overflow checks.

summary: Touched this pass only for a factual API-surface correction: the code sample's scalar depthType member (not defined by the spec) is now the spec's depthTypeRequest: ["smooth"] ordered sequence, matching the immersive-web depth-sensing draft IDL verified today. The page itself — a labelled canvas simulation with a working raw/smooth/off toggle — was smoke-verified via CDP (toggle drives stats, clean console, no overflow on desktop or mobile) but not exhaustively re-reviewed; the 2026-06-01 critique's missing-edge-cases finding still stands, and telemetry, XR feature detection, and non-visual state remain gaps.
